questions: Can a system retain broad language-model coverage while making its consequential inferences machine-checkable?

direction.question: Can a system retain broad language-model coverage while making its consequential inferences machine-checkable?
direction.closureCriteria: On a predeclared suite spanning mathematics, repository-scale software verification, and structured domain rules, report proof coverage, proof-check success, residual unverified claims, abstentions, and capability loss relative to an otherwise matched unconstrained model.
partialResults: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 demonstrates strong formal mathematics performance in Lean 4.
LeanDojo and ReProver make retrieval-augmented theorem proving reproducible at laboratory scale.
VeriSoftBench shows that mathematics-specialized provers transfer poorly to dependency-rich software repositories.
starters: Individual: Build a proof-coverage auditor for a 7B prover on LeanDojo and VeriSoftBench that separates verified conclusions, unsupported premises, failed proofs, and timeouts.
Small lab: Train and evaluate one prover across mathematics and repository-scale software, explicitly measuring transfer loss and dependency-retrieval failures.
Well-funded lab: Develop a proof-carrying general assistant whose high-consequence outputs compile into multiple formal backends, with calibrated abstention when formalization is incomplete.

noveltyReview.scope: arXiv and official repositories for neural theorem proving, Lean, proof-carrying generation, repository-scale software verification, and neuro-symbolic reasoning.
noveltyReview.note: Formal mathematics is a strong and crowded subfield, but broad cross-domain machine-checkable inference remains incomplete; no priority claim is made.

counterexamples: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B reports 88.9 percent on MiniF2F and solves 49 of 658 PutnamBench problems.
LeanDojo and ReProver provide open data, tooling, retrieval, and a 98,734-theorem benchmark.
FormalMATH, Leanabell-Prover-V2, and Lean Copilot provide additional narrow formal-reasoning systems.
